g.text: HDR and ML + mask reach NRMSE 0.053 / 0.053 vs 0.032 for the single exposure at 16 bit, so neither 8-bit HDR result reaches the 16-bit single exposure.

text.style: fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: Findings: the published ML-HDR Eq. 14–15 keeps saturated samples, so its fused diffraction rate deviates from the noiseless rate (8-bit diffraction NRMSE 0.82) and its object NRMSE stays 0.18–0.23 at every bit depth. At 8 bit, LRFC-style

text.style: fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start
fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: n = 3 seeds per point: mean ± sample SD (error bars). Letters A–D mark the 8-bit results shown in (d). Where markers coincide, the smaller green triangles are drawn over the blue diamonds. Gray dashed line = our single exposure at 16 bit.

text.tspan: object-amplitude NRMSE = ‖|O|−|O|‖/‖|O|‖. The paper's RMS error definition is unspecified.

Cameraman object; read noise 5 e; single = one exposure at the auto-exposure time; HDR methods fuse all 7 exposures (0.5–500 ms). Metrics vs ground truth on the scanned ROI after a global complex-scalar and sub-pixel-shift alignment;

text.style: fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start
fill: #333333; font: 8.6px 'Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: Adapted simulation: our detector, object sampling and propagation distance differ from the paper; parameters are recorded in meta.json. Our LRFC-style linear-response baseline selects the longest unsaturated exposure per pixel; this selection
